claims.text: The initial as-cast MoNbTaW alloy is single phase.
The initial as-cast MoNbTaW alloy has a homogeneous composition.
Heating MoNbTaW at approximately 1000°C for 2 hours followed by rapid quenching will produce a dual-phase microstructure.
The proposed heat treatment will form uniformly distributed coherent nano-precipitates in the MoNbTaW matrix.
In situ monitoring will enable control of precipitate size and uniformity.
The coherent nano-precipitates will act as preferential sinks for irradiation-induced vacancies and interstitials.
Defect absorption at the nano-precipitates will enhance vacancy-interstitial recombination.
Enhanced defect recombination will limit irradiation-induced swelling.
Coherent precipitates will minimize stress concentrations.
Minimizing stress concentrations will preserve alloy ductility.
Minimizing stress concentrations will preserve alloy yield strength.
After irradiation at approximately 800°C to as much as 10 dpa, the heat-treated alloy will exhibit more than a 25% improvement in defect recombination efficiency relative to the as-cast control.
After irradiation, the heat-treated alloy will exhibit less swelling than the as-cast control.
After irradiation, the heat-treated alloy will maintain its yield strength relative to the as-cast control.
Unmodified as-cast MoNbTaW accumulates more irradiation-induced defects than the proposed heat-treated alloy.
Unmodified as-cast MoNbTaW exhibits greater irradiation-induced swelling than the proposed heat-treated alloy.
Unmodified as-cast MoNbTaW undergoes subtle degradation of mechanical properties after irradiation.
The proposed benefit depends on achieving a uniform precipitate distribution.
